page: Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are included.

In benchmark evaluations, this instance demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core testing. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range. Memory performance is highly competitive, with PassMark memory scores reaching the top 10% and large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25%. Single-threaded data processing is strong, as evidenced by top 25% results in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. For specialized workloads, the server delivers strong text generation speeds during LLM inference with small 135M models, while medium 7B model inference and database operations perform at average levels.

The server offers a balanced resource profile with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, aligning with general-purpose and moderately compute-intensive requirements. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high-speed NVMe storage provides reliable performance without resource contention. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate machine learning inference tasks that do not require GPU acceleration.
description: Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks a GPU. It delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and top-tier memory scores in PassMark testing, alongside strong large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression speeds. Multi-core performance, database operations, and web serving throughput remain in the average tier. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, database management, and light LLM inference tasks.
